rows.grounds: sandhi fusion of tasya and icchā; refers to the will of that agent
abstract condition of becoming an effect or object of action
past participle indicating attainment of a state
relative pronoun referring to the will as instrumental cause
sandhi fusion of saḥ and icchaḥ; identifies the arisen will
fused token expressing the arising or birth of that will

items.question: How does will attain effectuation and thereby bring itself into arising?
premises: A prior will belongs to the agent in the sequence of action.
That will attains the state of being effectuated.
By that same will, the will arises as an operative impulse.
items.inference: Will functions both as what becomes effectuated and as the means by which operative will comes into being.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tasya may be the agent or a preceding mental state.
items.plain_english: When that will reaches the state of being carried out, it is by that will that the operative will comes into being.
